At the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law, scholars pursue research relating to fundamental issues and current developments in the areas of public international law, European Union law, and the constitutional and administrative law of individual states, together with numerous visiting scholars from all over the world. In its fields, our library is the largest in Europe and one of the most comprehensive in the world.The newly established Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER), headed by Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, invites applications for twoResearch Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m)with a preferred starting date of 1 January 2027 (the positions are funded for three years)The Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER) investigates how global order is transformed as states - particularly great and middle powers - pursue competing visions of the principles, rules and institutions that structure international relations amid intensifying geopolitical rivalry. The group conceptualizes these processes as constellations of global (dis)ordering through which states seek to advance their visions of order by creating, reshaping, connecting, bypassing, or disengaging from international institutions, building new formal or ad hoc institutional arrangements, and strategically leveraging economic and technological interdependence. DISORDER examines how such constellations emerge across the fields of security, economy, and technology, and what forms of global order they produce, transform, or erode.Job descriptionThe successful candidates will develop independent doctoral dissertation projects within the framework of the Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER). Their research should contribute to the group’s broader inquiry into how states pursue competing visions of global order through international institutions and how these processes reshape global order across different issue areas.Possible orientations of the doctoral projects include:- an actor-centred perspective, examining how a particular great or middle power pursues its vision of global order across different issue areas institutional settings; or- a domain-centred perspective, comparing how different states interact with and reshape international institutions within a particular field, such as security, economy, or technology.Potential empirical cases may include, but are not limited to, the United States, China, Russia, India, Brazil, Japan, and other international actors such as the European Union.The doctoral researchers will:- develop and conduct an original PhD project that contributes to the conceptual and empirical agenda of the DISORDER research group;- conduct empirical research using qualitative methods such as process tracing, qualitative content and discourse analysis, and semi-structured interviews;- contribute to the comparative and collaborative research activities of the group;- participate in research group meetings, workshops, conferences, and other academic activities;- present research findings at international conferences and prepare publications for peer-reviewed academic outlets;- contribute to the organization of workshops, conferences, and other activities of the research group and the MPIL.Your profile- An excellent Master’s degree or equivalent in Political Science, with a specialization in International Relations or Foreign Policy Analysis- A strong research interest in global order, international institutions, and great- and middle-power politics, including their foreign policies- A substantive interest in one or more of the group’s empirical issue areas (security, economy, and technology)- A strong interest in qualitative research and familiarity with relevant research methods- Excellent written and spoken English- Additional language skills and country- or region-specific expertise relevant to the proposed doctoral project are considered assets- The ability to conduct independent research while contributing actively to a collaborative research environmentWe offer- An attractive and international work environment with an unparalleled research infrastructure and a good working atmosphere- A varied, responsible and team-orientated job- Remuneration in accordance with the guidelines of the MPG funding agreements (65 per cent of EG13, TVöD-Bund)- Access to our world-leading library and a multitude of databases- A workplace that is easy to reach by public transport and free employee parking spaces- A job ticket for public transport- Offers for work-life balance and four affiliated daycare centresApplicationThe Max Planck Society has set itself the goal of employing more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged. The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore strongly encouraged to apply.Interested candidates are invited to submit their complete application exclusively via the online application system (https://jobs.mpil.de/3vrp7) available on our website by 22 November 2026.Applications should include a CV, a cover letter of no more than two pages, copies of relevant degree certificates and transcripts of records, a one-page summary of the applicant’s Master’s thesis, a five-page PhD project proposal that clearly relates to the research agenda of the DISORDER group and indicates which of the thematic orientations outlined above the proposed project primarily addresses, and two letters of recommendationThe documents will be deleted after the application process. The interviews will take place in late November/early December in person at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg. Application expenses cannot be covered.For questions regarding the positions, please contact Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at friedrichs@mpil.de (https://mailto:friedrichs@mpil.de) .

We, the Max Planck Institute for Medical Research, are one of 85 institutes and research centers of the Max Planck Society (MPG) for the advancement of science. Our focus is on basic medical research. We currently employ around 270 people in science and administration, mainly at our location in Heidelberg. Another location for our institute is currently being established in Heilbronn. We are also part of the Health + Life Science Alliance Heidelberg Mannheim, an association of the region's leading life science research institutions.The MPG strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. As the MPG has set itself the goal of employing more people with severe disabilities, applications from people with severe disabilities are expressly welcome. In addition, the MPG wants to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore expressly encouraged to apply.The female reproductive tract is a highly dynamic system in which tissue mechanics, active forces, and fluid flow interact with cellular and physiological processes. Yet, how these physical properties contribute to reproductive function remains poorly understood.Within the ERC Starting Grant project REPROMECH – Quantitative Mechanics of the Oviduct: Force, Flow, and the Physiological Operating Point, our group investigates how forces and mechanical properties shape the function of the female reproductive system. We combine approaches from reproductive biology, mechanobiology, and experimental biophysics to quantitatively characterize living tissues across cellular and tissue scales.The doctoral project will investigate the mechanical properties of the female reproductive tract and their relationship to tissue function.Tasks- Quantification of mechanical properties of the female reproductive tract using complementary mechanical measurements and advanced microscopy- Preparation and culture of ex vivo tissue samples- Histological characterization of biological samples- Quantitative image and data analysis- Critical analysis and interpretation of experimental resultsProfile- You hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in reproductive biology, developmental biology, biology, biophysics, physics, bioengineering, biomedical engineering, biotechnology, or a related discipline.- We are looking for a candidate with strong experimental aptitude, excellent practical laboratory skills, manual dexterity, and a quantitative and analytical mindset.- You should enjoy technically demanding experimental work, be able to interpret complex data critically and rigorously, and be motivated to work across disciplinary boundaries.- Willingness to work with laboratory mice and to complete the required laboratory-animal training is essential.- Previous experience in reproductive biology, experimental biophysics, microscopy, or work with laboratory animals is advantageous but not required. Candidates with a background in reproductive biology and an interest in quantitative and biophysical approaches are particularly encouraged to apply.- Excellent communication skills in written and spoken English are required.Our offerThe position is funded for an initial period of three years within the ERC Starting Grant REPROMECH, with the possibility of extension, and is available from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible.We offer a vibrant international research environment, access to state-of-the-art infrastructure for quantitative microscopy and mechanobiology, and opportunities for scientific training and conference participation.Remuneration: 75% of pay group E13 under TVöD Bund.We look forward to receiving your application, including a cover letter, curriculum vitae, copies of relevant degree certificates and transcripts, and contact details of two academic referees. Applications must be submitted electronically via the application portal (https://bewerbermanagement.net/en/jobposting/5572b068e91236d723de14e45b3737686f35fab70/apply) by 1 November 2026.For further information, please contact Dr. Stephanie Möllmert (stephanie.moellmert@mr.mpg.de (https://mailto:stephanie.moellmert@mr.mpg.de) ).For general questions, please contact Ms. Julia Gauglitz (julia.gauglitz@mr.mpg.de (https://mailto:julia.gauglitz@mr.mpg.de) ) from human resources.

Serco is an international provider of services to governments and public organisations, operating across sectors where delivery, public confidence and reputation matter. This role is the senior local communications lead for EHC in Germany and leads internal communications for ORS in Switzerland, while working as an integral member of the European Communications team.The postholder will have the autonomy to shape and deliver communications locally, working closely with local leaders and drawing on the expertise and support of the European Communications team. The role calls for sound judgement, curiosity and a practical approach to strengthening employee understanding, engagement and reputation as EHC and ORS continue their journey within Serco.Key purpose  - Lead communications for EHC in Germany across internal and external channels, ensuring communications are accurate, relevant and appropriate for a sensitive public-service environment.- Own internal communications for ORS in Switzerland, helping leaders keep employees informed, engaged and connected to local priorities and Serco’s wider direction.- Act as a trusted communications adviser to the EHC and ORS leadership teams, providing clear, practical and well-judged counsel, including in complex, sensitive or fast-moving situations.- Build strong networks across the local businesses and Serco Europe, connecting people, expertise and information so communications are coordinated and effective.- Support the continued integration of EHC and ORS within Serco, respecting their local identities while embedding Serco’s communications standards, governance, channels and values.Structure and reporting relationship The role reports to the Customer Relations (CR) & Operations Director Switzerland. The postholder is also a core member of the European Communications team and works closely with the Director of Communications, Marketing and Public Affairs Europe and European Communications colleagues on priorities, standards, governance and delivery. The role operates with a high degree of independence and works closely with EHC leadership in Germany and ORS leadership in Switzerland.  Internal Communications- Own and deliver the internal communications plans for EHC in Germany and ORS in Switzerland, including print and digital newsletters, leadership updates, employee announcements, change communications and internal campaigns, working closely with local leaders and the European Communications team.- Draft and distribute newsletters; act as an internal correspondent to identify and write impactful stories.- Lead employee engagement initiatives aligned with Serco’s values and business priorities.- Develop and maintain content for internal platforms.  External Communications- Lead day-to-day media relations in Germany and preferably Switzerland, including media monitoring, handling enquiries, preparing spokespeople and coordinating responses with European Communications colleagues when required.- Lead local issues management and crisis communications preparedness, providing calm, practical and well-judged advice to leaders in sensitive or difficult situations.- Produce clear written and visual content for external channels, including social media, in line with European Communications standards and priorities.- Manage the German-speaking  website of Immigration Europe and related external digital content for Germany and Switzerland, in line with European Communications standards and approvals.Integration Communications- Contribute to integration plans following recent acquisitions, ensuring employees and stakeholders are informed and engaged.- Apply strong change communications judgement, identifying how different audiences may respond to change and adapting messages, channels and engagement approaches to their needs and sensitivities.Social Media & Content Creation- Collaborate with the European communications team to source, create, and promote content that showcases services, people, and impact.Stakeholder Engagement- Build and sustain trusted relationships across operations, HR, corporate functions and leadership teams, creating effective networks within EHC in Germany, ORS in Switzerland and the wider European business.- Represent the European Communications function locally. Act as a trusted communications adviser to EHC leaders in Germany across the full communications remit and to ORS leaders in Switzerland on internal communications, constructively challenging proposed approaches where reputational, employee or stakeholder considerations require it.- For German-speaking market, develop and maintain strong working relationships with relevant media, partners, public authorities and other external stakeholders, supported by accurate and well-maintained contact information and external specialist partners.Essential technical and professional skills, knowledge, and qualifications - Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.- At least seven years’ relevant communications experience, including substantial responsibility for advising senior leaders, managing communications independently and delivering through influence in a complex, matrixed organisation.- Proven experience across internal communications, external communications, media relations, change communications and employee engagement.- Strong change management and change communications acumen, with the ability to understand audience sensitivities, anticipate resistance and translate complex change into clear, relevant communications.- Excellent planning and organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise competing demands across two businesses and maintain consistent delivery.- Demonstrable experience of working with journalists, handling media enquiries and advising spokespeople, with the judgement to manage sensitive or high-pressure situations.- Strong digital communications capability, including confident use of Microsoft 365, SharePoint and content management tools.- Ability to brief and manage specialist creative support when needed, ensuring outputs meet communications objectives and brand standards.- Able to navigate a large, matrixed company while remaining pragmatic, visible and hands-on within smaller subsidiaries. Comfortable balancing accountability to a local operational leader with active membership of a European functional team, adapting style without compromising communications standards.- Sound understanding of, or experience in, public services, immigration, social care, government or another sensitive, regulated operating environment.Additional / special features of the role - Highly self-sufficient and dependable, with the judgement to set priorities, make sound decisions, escalate appropriately and maintain delivery without close supervision.- Credible, politically aware and collaborative, with the interpersonal confidence to build networks, sustain trusted relationships and influence colleagues from operational teams to senior leadership.- Inclusive and audience-focused, prepared to reach beyond familiar channels and proactively engage employees and stakeholders with different roles, backgrounds, levels of access and communications needs.- Calm and resilient in demanding or ambiguous environments, able to handle sensitive issues, challenge constructively, protect confidentiality and maintain effective relationships during difficult situations.- Tech-savvy and adaptable to new digital tools and platforms.- Interested in the evolution of the immigration market in Europe, incl. the politicial impact on the business of the Sector Immigration EuropeDesirable- Must: German native or fully proficient- Must: English level B2- Desirable: French- Experience in regulated environments or public sector communications.Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

Tätigkeitsbereich: IT/TelekommunikationFachabteilung: Payment-related ProductsGesellschaft: Mercedes pay GmbHStandort: BerlinStartdatum: 01.06.2026Veröffentlichungsdatum: 01.06.2026Stellennummer: MER00044HAArbeitszeit: Full timeAufgabenWHAT WE DOPicture the car of the future. Does it fly? Does it look like the one from that famous 80s movie?We believe the car of the future is already here—and it’s a connected vehicle that can be used as a payment device. Here at Mercedes pay, we enable seamless, secure, and trustworthy payments across the entire Mercedes-Benz ecosystem. We develop sleek new payment products & solutions to provide customers with an effortless, convenient user experience; not just via an app or web browser, but even in-car. The car as a payment device? We made it happen!Mercedes-Benz is known for its legacy, but innovation and legacy are not mutually exclusive—quite the contrary. Our mission is to empower innovation within one of the top luxury car brands worldwide, helping it continue to pioneer the automotive industry. To sum it up, we are the FinTech branch or knowledge hub for payments within Mercedes-Benz.ABOUT MERCEDES PAYMercedes pay launched in its first market in 2018 and is now active in more than 40 countries on five continents, enabling transaction processing for Mercedes-Benz products and services. Depending on the market, Mercedes pay may act as the technical payment gateway for transaction processing from Mercedes me store, the Mercedes me app, in-car payments and may even support online vehicle sales. This is how Mercedes pay directly contributes to the mobility and digitalization strategy of Mercedes-Benz Group AG. Mercedes pay is a wholly owned subsidiary of Mercedes-Benz AG with offices in Berlin, Stuttgart, and Farmington Hills (USA).2023 has already been a big year—we launched full online vehicle payments in the UK and introduced native in-car payments in Germany, an industry-first feature by which users can pay directly by fingerprint inside their car. That’s the car of the future we’re talking about!OUR VALUES & HOW WE WORKWe are an inclusive, passionate, and diverse team of people. Being solution-oriented, agile, and dynamic is in our blood. We learn best by leaping into cold water from time to time, by doing rather than deliberating, and we trust in our teammates’ abilities & willingness to learn. We like to make things happen, and we’re more interested in finding solutions than sulking at inconveniences.Since we are still building new processes alongside new products, new joiners have the opportunity to make as much impact as our most seasoned veterans. We really love a lively exchange of ideas, whether a teammate’s been with us for two days or ten years. And, frankly, fresh energy is always welcome. YOUR DAY AT GLANCEYou assess current systems, infrastructure, and business processes to identify improvement opportunities and ensure compatibility with new solutions- You collect and analyze stakeholder requirements to define solution scope and objectives- You architect the Mercedes Pay Digital Voucher Solution, detailing structure, components, interfaces, and data flows, and select suitable technologies, platforms, and tools- You create proof-of-concept projects to validate solutions and demonstrate feasibility- You work with an experienced team of Solution Architects as well as the company's Enterprise, Cloud and Security Architects to derive right-fit solutions- You facilitate the collaboration with external development teams, ensuring adherence to architectural guidelines and best practices- You communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, translating complex technical details into accessible language- You document solutions and disseminate best practices among team membersQualifikationenWHAT YOU BRING TO THE TABLE- You hold a degree in Computer Science or a related field- You have 5+ years of experience as a Solution Architect, with a strong focus on software product development- You have practical experience in at least one of the following domains: regulatory environments, agentic commerce, loyalty programs, vouchers, digital marketing, or payments (including PCI DSS, PSD2/SCA, or AML/KYC)- You are proficient in microservices, event-driven architectures, cloud-native technologies (e.g., Kubernetes, CI/CD), Auth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocols, alongside practices like Domain-Driven Design (DDD) and DevOps- You have hands-on experience with tools such as Jira, GitHub, and Datadog- You have a proven track record of implementing cutting-edge technologies within a corporate environment- You possess strong teamwork and good communication skills, with the ability to maintain composure under pressure- You are fluent in English; Does it fly? Does it look like the one from that famous 80s movie?We believe the car of the future is already here—and it’s a connected vehicle that can be used as a payment device. Here at Mercedes pay, we enable seamless, secure, and trustworthy payments across the entire Mercedes-Benz ecosystem. We develop sleek new payment products & solutions to provide customers with an effortless, convenient user experience; not just via an app or web browser, but even in-car. The car as a payment device? We made it happen!Mercedes-Benz is known for its legacy, but innovation and legacy are not mutually exclusive—quite the contrary. Depending on the market, Mercedes pay may act as the technical payment gateway for transaction processing from Mercedes me store, the Mercedes me app, in-car payments and may even support online vehicle sales. This is how Mercedes pay directly contributes to the mobility and digitalization strategy of Mercedes-Benz Group AG. jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day Join us as a FACTS Solution Architect (SA) and become a pivotal part of our organization! You will drive early technical engagement with customers, operators, and regulators, ensuring our solutions align with our portfolio while introducing innovative technologies. By analyzing customer needs from the outset, you will guide the development of advanced and commercially viable solutions. Collaborating closely with Sales, Tendering, and Product Lifecycle Management, you will ensure seamless integration of expertise from the very beginning. Your proactive communication style will foster a positive project team spirit, encouraging others to share in the excitement of achieving common goals.How You’ll Make an Impact * Define and review technical requirements, ensuring alignment on performance, interfaces, and standards* Be involved in early technical engagement with customers, operators, and regulators to align solutions and promote new technologies* Support grid planning and integration, contributing to future concepts and expansion strategies* Lead and coordinate technical solution development during the pre-acquisition and tender phase across international teams* Collaborate with Sales and Tender teams on market development, bids, and pre-acquisition activities* Analyze market trends, support solution development with PLM teams, and contribute to industry standards and thought leadership (e.g., IEEE)What You Bring* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical field* Extensive engineering experience, preferably in FACTS technology* Knowledge of power system and network stability analysis* Experience with international technical standardization is an advantage* Strong analytical, communication, and interpersonal skills for working in multicultural environments* Proficiency in negotiation, teamwork, leadership, and excellent English skills (German is a plus) About the TeamOur Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology.  Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits * In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs#RPO
